subject: Moon surface
title: What If You Were Buried on the Moon? So Far, Exactly One Person Is

scenes.text: What if you were buried on the Moon? One man is, and he never got to go alive.
Gene Shoemaker taught Apollo astronauts about craters and hoped to walk on the Moon himself. Addison's disease grounded him.
He co-discovered the comet that hit Jupiter in 1994. In 1997 he died in a car accident in Australia, hunting craters.
A colleague had an idea. One ounce of his ashes rode aboard NASA's Lunar Prospector, launched in January 1998.
The capsule was wrapped in brass foil etched with a comet, a crater, and lines from Romeo and Juliet.
On July 31, 1999, its mission done, NASA crashed the probe near the Moon's south pole. So far, he's the only person laid to rest on another world.

description:
What if you were buried on the Moon? One ounce of the ashes of geologist Eugene Shoemaker, who trained Apollo astronauts and co-discovered Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9, rode aboard NASA's Lunar Prospector, launched on 6 January 1998.
Addison's disease had ended his own hopes of going. When the probe's mission ended on 31 July 1999 it was deliberately crashed near the lunar south pole at about 3,800 miles an hour, capsule and all.
What should we run through next?

first_comment: The foil carried lines from Romeo and Juliet about being cut into little stars. Where in the solar system would you want to rest?
